title: Göbeklitepe and Şanlıurfa: How to Plan the Visit, Ticket by Ticket
excerpt: Opening hours, the €20 Göbeklitepe ticket that also covers Karahantepe, how far the sites are from Şanlıurfa and the airport, and a one- or two-day plan that adds the Archaeology Museum and Harran without wasted driving.

body.text: Göbeklitepe is one of the few places in Türkiye where people fly in for a single site. Its stone enclosures and T-shaped pillars date from the Pre-Pottery Neolithic, roughly 9600–8200 BCE according to the [UNESCO World Heritage listing](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1572/), so they predate pottery and belong to the era when hunter-gatherers were moving towards the first farming communities. Allow time for the site itself, plus travel. Getting the logistics right around it is what decides whether the trip feels easy or rushed: which ticket to buy, when the gates close, how to reach a hilltop 15 km outside the city, and what else in Şanlıurfa deserves your time.
This guide uses the Ministry of Culture and Tourism's own site pages (checked on 15 November 2026) for hours and fees, and is clear where official information is missing or ambiguous.

items: Location: about 15 km north-east of Şanlıurfa city, near Örencik village (official [Göbeklitepe page](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=SGT01&DistId=SGT)).
Hours: 08:30–17:30 every day; the ticket office closes at 17:00. The ministry page shows no separate winter timetable.
Ticket: €20 for foreign visitors, and the page states that this ticket is also valid for entry to Karahantepe.

Other sites in a typical plan: Karahantepe (Haliliye district), Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum (in the city) and Harran (44 km south), all listed at 08:30–17:30 with the box office closing at 17:00. The Harran page shows no fee and an ambiguous 'Closed' label; confirm before driving out.
Fees are revised periodically; see [our 2027 museum fee planner](/blog/turkiye-museum-site-fees-2027) before you budget a 2027 trip.

body.text: Which ticket do you actually need?

For most visitors the answer is one Göbeklitepe ticket. The ministry page for Göbeklitepe gives €20 and says it is valid for Karahantepe too, so there is no reason to buy Karahantepe separately if you plan to see both. The [Karahantepe page](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=KRH01&DistId=MRK) lists a €3 ticket that it says is also valid for Göbeklitepe; at our check its fee line also carried the word "closed", so treat Karahantepe's status as something to confirm on the day rather than assume.

The ministry also sells a combined product that pairs the archaeological site with a Göbeklitepe animation area, but its [catalogue entry](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MUS23-87-008) gives no price or detail, so we cannot tell you whether it is worth it. Museum passes are another question: the official [pass page](https://muze.gov.tr/museumpass) lists MuseumPass Türkiye and regional passes but does not name Göbeklitepe among covered sites, and MüzeKart is for Turkish citizens only. If you already hold a pass for a wider trip, ask at the ticket office; do not buy one only for Şanlıurfa on the assumption that it covers the site.

Şanlıurfa GAP Airport is roughly 35 km from the city centre; a local news guide citing the airports authority for the distance puts the drive at about 30–40 minutes and the airport shuttle at about 45 minutes ([Urfanatik, July 2026](https://www.urfanatik.com/gap-havalimani-ile-sanliurfa-arasi-kac-km-arabayla-kac-saat-otobusle-kac-saat-surer)). The same source says municipal buses link the airport with a stop at the Göbeklitepe Abide junction in the city; there is no official public transport to the site itself. Karahantepe is about 55 km from central Şanlıurfa according to its official page, so most itineraries use a taxi, hire car or booked driver to combine the two sites.

A simple rule: if you only have one day, base yourself in the city and do the two Neolithic sites in the morning, when the hilltop is cooler in summer and the light is softer, then return for the museum after lunch.
A one-day and a two-day plan

items: One day: Göbeklitepe at opening (08:30), Karahantepe late morning if it is open (allow roughly an hour's drive each way), lunch in the city, Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum in the afternoon, Balıklıgöl and the old bazaar area at dusk.
Two days: day one as above but slower; day two to Harran (44 km south, same 08:30–17:30 hours) and back for an evening in the city.
Arriving by air the same morning: go straight to the museum or Harran and leave Göbeklitepe for the next day's first slot, so you are not racing the 17:00 ticket-office cut-off.
Combining with Gaziantep: Şanlıurfa pairs well with a [Gaziantep food weekend](/blog/gaziantep-food-weekend-planning); plan Göbeklitepe on the Şanlıurfa day with the most daylight.

body.text: Do not skip the Archaeology Museum

The [Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=SUM02&DistId=SUM) is open daily 08:30–17:30 and shows €10 for admission. Many finds from the region's Neolithic sites are displayed here, which helps the hilltop make sense once you see the pillars in situ. The Haleplibahçe Mosaic Museum is in a separate building in the same garden; the ministry page does not say whether the €10 ticket covers it, so check at the desk.

November to March is quieter and the midday sun is less punishing, which suits a site with little shade. The trade-off is weather. Karahantepe was closed temporarily for heavy rain and strong wind early in 2026 and had reopened by 4 March 2026, as [Sabah reported](https://www.sabah.com.tr/sanliurfa/2026/03/04/karahantepe-yeniden-ziyaretcilere-kapilarini-acti). On a wet or windy forecast, check the site's status before driving out and keep the museum day flexible. Bring a layer: the hilltop is exposed.

items: Reach the Göbeklitepe ticket office before 17:00; earlier is better in summer.
Buy the €20 Göbeklitepe ticket and keep it for Karahantepe.
Confirm Karahantepe is open on the day; the official listing was ambiguous at our check.
Arrange transport that links both Neolithic sites; buses alone will not.
Re-check fees close to your travel date.

seo.intent: Traveller planning a visit to Göbeklitepe from Şanlıurfa wants hours, the right ticket, transport and how to fit in Karahantepe, the Archaeology Museum and Harran.
keywords: how to get to Gobekli Tepe
seo.uniqueValue: Uses the ministry's own site pages to explain that one €20 Göbeklitepe ticket covers Karahantepe, flags what the official pages leave unclear (pass coverage, Karahantepe status, combined ticket), and turns hours and distances into one- and two-day plans.

quality.reviewNotes: Independent fact-check 2026-11-15 (separate agent opened all nine sources: four muze.gov.tr site pages, museumpass page, combined-ticket catalogue entry, UNESCO 1572, Sabah 2026-03-04, Urfanatik). Hours 08:30-17:30/17:00, €20 ticket valid for Karahantepe, €3 Karahantepe ticket and its ambiguous 'Closed' label, €10 museum, Harran 44 km and ambiguous label, ~55 km to Karahantepe, airport distance attribution confirmed. Fixes applied: UNESCO framing narrowed, bus stop corrected to the city junction, unsourced Haleplibahçe combined-ticket claim removed, 'fees change every 1 April' removed, Harran status caveat added, travel-time realism added. Reviewer pre-fix score 72. Risk low: travel logistics only. No first-hand visit claimed. MuseumPass coverage of Göbeklitepe left explicitly unverified. Localization: DE, zh-CN, KO, ES written by separate agents and reviewed block by block by another independent agent (2026-11-15); two fixes applied (zh-CN three-year rule wording, KO fee-estimate scope); no omissions or number changes found.
